decisions.reason: Step 2.2 falsely identifies failure of U1 with the sum leaving the future cone: (2,0,0,0)+(-1,0,0,0) is future timelike despite -2<2. The independent computations -34<16 and 1<sqrt(2) already refute U1 and U2, so the defect is nonfatal. Repaired only the extraneous equivalence, preserving both witnesses and Statement refuted.

Definition (a) asserted inertial-worldline closure under all subinterval restrictions, but a singleton J=[0,0] has fewer than the two domain elements required by the curve definition and no defined quotient derivative. Added the necessary at-least-two-elements condition, the reanchored formula x(s)=x(t0)+(s-t0)d on J, and the singleton exclusion; preserved all nondegenerate inertial and piecewise inertial claims.

The Statement and Given assume a future timelike worldline in the exact weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline. Its Worldlines clause explicitly requires future timelike one-sided quotient tangents at both endpoints of every piece; thus those tangents are nonzero future causal and satisfy the integrability supplier. The example y(s)=(s^2,0,0,0) on [0,1] has zero tangent at 0 and is not such a worldline. F1 states consequences of the assumed worldline rather than replacing its definition.

The clock postulate defines C(b)-C(a) and leaves C(a) arbitrary, so neither absolute readings 2T and 2T/gamma nor the final traveler-behind ordering followed from the original setup. For example initial traveler reading 3T reverses the ordering. The repaired preparation sets both maps to zero at p, and steps 2.2-2.3 derive their increments before using those initial settings; geometry and proper-time values are preserved.
